re_line: Xi declares 'turnaround' with Albanese at APEC · Rio Tinto pledges $370m for Panguna · NZDF confirms cyber breach · US sanctions Comanchero gang · Cook Islands, Tonga declare states of emergency
morning_memo: Xi Jinping declared a 'comprehensive turnaround' in China-Australia ties at APEC even as Albanese publicly rebuked Vladimir Putin over Ukraine and defended appearing in Putin's group photograph.
Rio Tinto pledged $370 million to remediate its Panguna mine in Bougainville, addressing a toxic legacy tied to a civil war that killed an estimated 10,000 to 15,000 people.
The New Zealand Defence Force took its websites offline after a breach exposed names and emails tied to its Force4Families discount scheme, and has notified the Privacy Commissioner.

top_stories.headline: Xi declares 'turnaround' with Australia as Albanese defends Putin rebuke
top_stories.body: Chinese President **Xi Jinping** told **Anthony Albanese** that relations between Beijing and Canberra have undergone a comprehensive turnaround, meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen despite ongoing tension over iron ore. Albanese separately defended his direct rebuke of Russian President Vladimir Putin, saying he told Putin "he needs to stop his war, and he needs to stop it now." Albanese also defended joining Putin in APEC's group photograph, citing respect for host China.
top_stories.src_line: per SMH (Natassia Chrysanthos): "Xi wants stronger bonds with Australia as Albanese defends Putin rebuke" · also Reuters

top_stories.headline: Rio Tinto pledges $370 million for Panguna mine legacy in Bougainville
top_stories.body: **Rio Tinto** will contribute *$370 million* over coming years to a new fund addressing the toxic legacy of its Panguna mine, nearly forty years after local opposition forced the 1989 closure that triggered a civil war killing an estimated 10,000 to 15,000 people. Chief safety and technical officer **Mark Davies** called the pledge an important milestone following an impact assessment that found mine waste and decaying infrastructure still affect thousands. Locals cited clean water and transport as immediate priorities.
top_stories.src_line: per ABC Pacific: "Bougainville landowners 'overwhelmed' at Rio Tinto's $370m pledge"

top_stories.headline: US Treasury sanctions Australia's Comanchero gang over cartel links
top_stories.body: The US Treasury imposed sanctions on the Comanchero outlaw motorcycle gang and five of its members over links to Mexican drug cartels, acting on intelligence the Australian Federal Police passed to US authorities. AFP Assistant Commissioner for Global Operations **Stephen Nutt** said the gang has been doing business with four Mexican cartels, including the Sinaloa cartel, and the sanctions would make the Comanchero "less attractive" to criminal partners.
top_stories.src_line: per Reuters: "US sanctions Australian Comanchero motorcycle gang over drug trafficking links" · also ABC Pacific

overnight_items.headline: Albanese's global dash pays off abroad, may miss at home
overnight_items.body_text: Analysis in the AFR argues **Anthony Albanese**'s APEC travel delivered tangible wins on Quad military exercises, fuel security, and top-level access in Beijing, even as viral criticism over summit spending and foreign fast food dents his standing at home. The piece frames the trip as a split verdict: diplomatic gains abroad, political cost domestically.

overnight_items.headline: Xi calls for 'open regionalism' to sustain Asia-Pacific growth
overnight_items.body_text: Chinese President **Xi Jinping** used his APEC address in Shenzhen to call for open regionalism to sustain Asia-Pacific economic growth, a pitch for free trade delivered as the summit's three-way Trump-Xi-Putin meeting drew more attention than its substance.

overnight_items.headline: Productivity Commission proposes reporting cuts to ease burden
overnight_items.body_text: The Productivity Commission has proposed cutting corporate reporting requirements to ease Australia's regulatory burden, per Capital Brief. Further detail on the scope of the proposed changes was not available in the report.

overnight_items.headline: Contested defence bill passes the Senate amid crossbench fury
overnight_items.body_text: A contested defence bill passed the Senate on Friday despite crossbench objections, per thepoint.com.au. The wire report did not detail the bill's specific provisions.

pacific_wire.headline: Cook Islands declares state of emergency for Nassau over Cyclone Xavier
pacific_wire.body_text: Cook Islands Prime Minister **Mark Brown** declared a state of emergency for Nassau Island as Tropical Cyclone Xavier approaches, with the Fiji Meteorological Service forecasting the storm to pass south of the island this weekend as a category 2 or 3 system. Nassau, home to fewer than 100 people, lies more than *1,100 kilometres* northwest of Rarotonga; the declaration empowers authorities to evacuate residents under the Disaster Risk Management Act 2007.

pacific_wire.headline: Tonga declares nationwide state of emergency as drought worsens
pacific_wire.body_text: Tonga has declared a nationwide state of emergency as an El Nino-driven drought worsens, per Islands Business' PACNEWS wire, as Pacific delegations at COP31 press for stronger climate finance commitments they say are needed for resilience.

pacific_wire.headline: Fiji's climate minister rejects COP31 draft text
pacific_wire.body_text: Fiji's Climate Change Minister **Tabuya** rejected the COP31 draft negotiating text, saying "we cannot accept it," per Islands Business' PACNEWS wire, as Pacific delegations in Antalya push back against language they say falls short on the 1.5-degree target.

pacific_wire.headline: Niue wins Earthshot Prize for ocean protection program
pacific_wire.body_text: Niue has won an Earthshot Prize for an ocean protection program, with a university official describing Pacific islands as "the vanguard of the solutions" to climate and environmental threats despite being on their frontline.

pacific_wire.headline: Activists condemn US missile test at Kwajalein Atoll
pacific_wire.body_text: An unarmed US intercontinental ballistic missile launched from California struck Kwajalein Atoll in the Marshall Islands, one of four annual US tests in the Pacific, drawing condemnation from regional anti-nuclear activists. **Reverend James Bhagwan**, General Secretary of the Pacific Conference of Churches, led activists to Parliament House calling on states to "rethink their strategy about using the Pacific as a testing ground."

pacific_wire.headline: Australia adds $1.75 million emergency aid for PNG drought
pacific_wire.body_text: Australia has committed an extra *$1.75 million* in emergency aid to Papua New Guinea as an El Nino-driven drought leaves Western Province communities struggling for water, on top of $7 million already announced in October. World Vision Australia will receive $750,000 of the new funding; CEO **Grant Bayldon** said the immediate focus is "getting the water flowing" while building longer-term supply solutions.

pacific_wire.headline: US awards first deep-sea mining lease near American Samoa
pacific_wire.body_text: The US government awarded its first-ever deep-sea mining lease, covering *31.5 million acres* near American Samoa, to Wetstone U.S. Ventures, the sole bidder in a livestreamed California auction that generated $6 million for a 20-year term with a structured royalty schedule. American Samoa's governor, previously opposed, welcomed what he called a "new era of exploration."

pacific_wire.headline: Vanuatu charts eye care overhaul amid outer-island gaps
pacific_wire.body_text: Vanuatu's eye healthcare system needs major structural investment to reach outer-island communities and curb preventable vision loss linked to diabetes, per Islands Business, highlighting persistent healthcare access gaps across the archipelago.

pacific_wire.headline: Pacific civil society holds the line on 1.5C at COP31
pacific_wire.body_text: Pacific civil society groups are maintaining pressure on the 1.5-degree target at COP31 in Antalya, six weeks after leaders and advocates gathered in Fiji for the Pacific Pre-COP, per Islands Business, as the Antalya talks wind toward a contested close.

new_zealand.headline: NZDF confirms database compromised, pulls websites offline
new_zealand.body_text: The **New Zealand Defence Force** confirmed a cybersecurity breach after its website provider reported unauthorised access on Friday morning, pulling affected sites offline pending a forensic investigation. Preliminary inquiries found a database tied to the Force4Families Defence Discounts scheme, containing registered users' names and email addresses, was accessed; the Privacy Commissioner has been notified and affected individuals warned to watch for phishing.

china_in_the_pacific.headline: Marape reassures Beijing after PNG's pacts with the West
china_in_the_pacific.body_text: PNG Prime Minister **Marape**'s government is moving to reassure Beijing after Papua New Guinea signed new security and economic pacts with the West, the Lowy Interpreter writes, arguing infrastructure funding, roads and gas revenue explain why Port Moresby intends to keep playing both sides of the China-US rivalry rather than choosing one.

canberra_politics.headline: Labor concedes to Greens to pass right-to-sue social media bill
canberra_politics.body_text: **Labor** has conceded to a key Greens demand in the Senate to advance legislation letting Australians sue social media companies for harm, though the Greens say the bill still needs "real teeth" before it secures their full support.

canberra_politics.headline: Speakman quits NSW parliament, warns against 'One Nation-lite'
canberra_politics.body_text: Former NSW Liberal leader **Mark Speakman** announced he will not recontest his seat of Cronulla, becoming the eighth Liberal MP to quit before the state election, and warned his party against becoming "One Nation-lite." Current leader **Kellie Sloane** said she "did everything" to keep him and believes the exodus has now ended.

canberra_politics.headline: Not the MP, but his wife defects to One Nation
canberra_politics.body_text: Nationals MP **Colin Boyce** had been watched for a possible defection to One Nation, but it was his wife, **Terri Boyce**, who switched allegiance from the LNP to One Nation, underscoring One Nation's inroads into Coalition ranks.

canberra_politics.headline: Taylor has stabilised the Libs, but can he reach the summit?
canberra_politics.body_text: **Angus Taylor** has stabilised the federal Liberal Party "at base camp" since taking the leadership, the SMH assesses, but will need to do "a heck of a lot better than 'OK'" to be competitive at the 2027 election despite promising early signs.

canberra_politics.headline: Nationals hope to retain Victorian seats ahead of One Nation
canberra_politics.body_text: The Nationals are hopeful of retaining all their Victorian seats, with internal figures showing the party has moved ahead of a surging One Nation in regional electorates ahead of this year's state poll, per The Australian.

business_economy.headline: Markets bet the RBA is done hiking; history says otherwise
business_economy.body_text: Markets are pricing an end to the **RBA**'s tightening cycle after the cash rate held at *4.35 percent* in August, but the AFR argues global parallels and still-sticky trimmed mean inflation, not expected back near the 2-to-3-percent target until late 2027, suggest further increases cannot be ruled out.

business_economy.headline: Economists warn of recession risk after jobless hike
business_economy.body_text: Economists are warning of recession risk after a jump in joblessness that The Australian describes as a major headache for Treasurer **Jim Chalmers** and **Anthony Albanese**, with the jobs shock feeding broader recession-risk signals.

business_economy.headline: Wellington-founded Morrison opens Abu Dhabi office
business_economy.body_text: Wellington-founded infrastructure investor **Morrison**, which counts New Zealand's Infratil among its clients and manages about *US$35 billion* in assets, has opened an Abu Dhabi office to deepen ties with Gulf sovereign investors, chief executive **Paul Newfield** said.

business_economy.headline: Peptide boom in Australia fuelled by illegal Chinese imports
business_economy.body_text: The number of Australians taking untested peptide injections to lose weight, build muscle, and extend their lifespan is surging through both legal and illegal channels, with the AFR reporting a black-market trade fuelled by illegal imports from China.

primary_documents.headline: Wong statement on ICJ Myanmar genocide ruling
primary_documents.body_text: Foreign Minister **Penny Wong** issued a statement responding to the International Court of Justice's ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, the court's first such finding against a state.

primary_documents.headline: Fifteen countries back UK and Australian settlement sanctions
primary_documents.body_text: Pakistan and fourteen other countries have backed sanctions imposed by the UK and Australia on Israeli settlements, according to Pakistan Today, signalling wider international alignment behind Canberra's settlement sanctions regime.

calendar_watch.event: Tropical Cyclone Xavier forecast to pass the Cook Islands
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: The Nassau state of emergency tests the Cook Islands' disaster response capacity on a remote outer island with fewer than 100 residents.
Pacific delegations are pressing to preserve the 1.5-degree target and climate finance commitments as the summit closes.
One Nation's polling surge and a potential record Greens result will test both major parties' Victorian base.
A deepening Liberal MP exodus, including former leader Mark Speakman, raises questions about the party's readiness for the poll.

key_stat.label: Rio Tinto's Panguna mine legacy fund pledge
key_stat.context: The pledge, made nearly 40 years after the mine's 1989 closure, targets environmental and social harms in Bougainville that advocates say have violated human rights.

also_today.headline: Study maps two untouched Marshall Islands ecosystems
also_today.body_text: Scientists have completed a comprehensive ecological study of Bikar and Bokak, two Marshall Islands atolls declared the country's first national marine sanctuary last year, finding them among the most intact ecosystems in the Pacific. Chief scientist **Alan Friedlander** said the atolls show "how far we've drifted away from the natural state."

also_today.headline: PNG matching ambition with climate action at COP31
also_today.body_text: Papua New Guinea's communities are already living the impacts of climate change as COP31 negotiators debate ambition in Antalya, Pacific Island Times reports, with drought and extreme weather increasingly shaping Port Moresby's climate diplomacy.

opeds_today.headline: Who commands, who answers? The legal accountability of foreign police in the Pacific
opeds_today.central_argument: A single Pacific policing body will not by itself resolve who is legally accountable when foreign police act abroad.
opeds_today.summary: Drawing on experience in Papua New Guinea and Solomon Islands, the piece argues that proposals for a unified Pacific policing framework do not resolve fundamental questions of command and legal responsibility when foreign officers operate in the region. It highlights accountability gaps across current bilateral and multilateral policing arrangements.
opeds_today.policy_so_what: Australia and partner states designing new Pacific policing initiatives need clear command and liability frameworks before deployment, not after an incident.

opeds_today.headline: By prodding Taiwan, Russia takes its alignment with China to new heights
opeds_today.central_argument: Russia is growing bolder in the Western Pacific by aligning more closely with China on Taiwan, and Australia and its partners should prepare for the implications.
opeds_today.summary: The piece notes that on November 17, two Russian bombers carried out an East Asian excursion into contested airspace near Taiwan, reflecting deepening Moscow-Beijing strategic alignment. It argues this signals Russia's growing willingness to needle Taiwan in coordination with Chinese positioning.
opeds_today.policy_so_what: Canberra should factor a more active Russian military presence in the Western Pacific into its own force posture and intelligence-sharing planning.

opeds_today.headline: Open-weight AI models need a 5G-style test on provenance
opeds_today.central_argument: Open-weight AI models require a provenance test modeled on the 5G security framework to manage cyber security risk.
opeds_today.summary: The Australian Signals Directorate's Australian Cyber Security Centre recently released two pieces of guidance on open-weight AI models, one on opportunities and cyber security risks, the second on broader governance questions. The author argues these models need a provenance test comparable to the scrutiny applied to 5G network equipment.
opeds_today.policy_so_what: Australian regulators face a near-term decision on whether to extend 5G-style supply chain vetting to AI model provenance across critical infrastructure.

opeds_today.headline: Gardens in distress: drought, pollution and deep-sea mining in New Ireland
opeds_today.central_argument: Drought is withering land gardens in New Ireland, Papua New Guinea, pushing communities toward ocean gardens that are themselves threatened by pollution and looming deep-sea mining.
opeds_today.summary: The field dispatch describes how communities in New Ireland are turning to marine resources as land-based food gardens fail under drought conditions. It warns that pollution and the prospect of deep-sea mining threaten the same waters now serving as a food security lifeline.
opeds_today.policy_so_what: Deep-sea mining approvals in Papua New Guinea's waters carry direct food security consequences for drought-stressed communities, a tradeoff regulators will need to weigh explicitly.
